findings: src/function/scalar/string/contains.cpp: this is a general Muła-style first+last byte substring search inside FindStrInStr. It uses SSE2 with a SWAR fallback and gates only on needle length >= 2 and haystack size <= 256. It never refers to a query, table, column or literal.

Bounds: with position_count = haystack_size - (needle_size-1), the highest byte any SSE2 or SWAR load reads is start+last_offset+15 (or +7), which is at most haystack_size-1. The overlapping final block shifts its mask by (i+B-position_count), which lands each bit on position i+j. No over-read and no position is skipped.

SWAR uses the exact zero-byte formula ~(((x&0x7F..)+0x7F..)|x|0x7F..), so it gives no false positives. Bits are visited low to high, so the leftmost match is returned, matching the old memchr+Contains<> path.

Edge cases behave correctly: an empty haystack, a needle longer than the haystack (returns INVALID_INDEX before the block search), needle_size==2 (the middle memcmp is skipped), and empty needles (handled by the caller). Big-endian and non-GCC builds keep the original path.
No cost is moved elsewhere, nothing in timing or measurement is touched, and the change is small and self-contained.
